title: bug: LogRotator.rotate() deletes the oldest activity-log generation and shifts the rest before it compresses the live log, so a failed or timed-out compression (a full disk, a locked file) leaves a 0-byte activity.log.1.gz, and since every append retries the rotation, five appends while it keeps failing wipe all five retained generations
description:
Filed by defect hunt #15 (task-928a468d), lane 3 (state persistence and the activity log). Verified at HEAD d5431577 in a git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout.

PROBLEM
- packages/moe-daemon/src/util/LogRotator.ts rotate() changes the generation chain before the new generation exists:
  - it unlinks activity.log.<retentionCount>.gz (:91-94);
  - it renames each .<i>.gz to .<i+1>.gz (:97-103);
  - only then does it compress the live log into .1.gz (:107) and truncate the live log (:110).
- When compressFile rejects, the chain is already damaged. compressFile rejects on a read, gzip or write stream error, such as ENOSPC or a Windows EPERM/EBUSY on the destination, and on the 30 s COMPRESSION_TIMEOUT_MS (:161-166). After that:
  - rejectOnce destroys the streams but never unlinks the partial destination (:139-159), so a 0-byte or truncated .1.gz stays behind;
  - the oldest generation is already deleted;
  - the live log is not truncated.
- rotateIfNeeded swallows the error and returns false (:71-74). But appendActivity calls it before EVERY append, inside the activity mutex (state/activityLog.ts:100-102). While the failure persists, each appended event repeats the whole cycle: one more good generation is deleted and replaced by a partial one, and the full live log is re-read and re-gzipped.

CONTRACT
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md:3167 (### moe.get_activity_log): "rotation keeps `LOG_RETENTION_COUNT` (default 5) generations".
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md:21: LOG_RETENTION_COUNT is the "Number of rotated logs to keep".
- state/activityLog.ts:203 relies on it: "LogRotator (util/LogRotator.ts) keeps activity.log.<n>.gz, newest n=1, contiguous". get_activity_log reads those generations (05a77c0d), and its reader stops at the first missing one (activityLog.ts:221).
- Sibling contract for the same class of write: util/atomicWrite.ts:11, "On any failure the temp file is cleaned up rather than leaked". atomicWrite never touches the target until the new bytes are fsynced.

EVIDENCE
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/me/zzHuntMe_rotateFailure.test.ts. Copy it into packages/moe-daemon/src/__hunt__/ of a d5431577 snapshot and run `npx vitest run src/__hunt__/zzHuntMe_rotateFailure.test.ts`.
- The test seeds activity.log.1-5.gz with gen-1 to gen-5 and a live log over the 1 MB threshold. It mocks zlib.createGzip with a stream that fails its first chunk with ENOSPC, then calls rotateIfNeeded(). Result: 2 failed.
  - One failed rotation: expected [gen-1 … gen-5]; received ["<unreadable 0B>", "gen-1", "gen-2", "gen-3", "gen-4"]. gen-5 is deleted and a 0-byte .1.gz is left behind.
  - Five failing appends: received ["<unreadable 0B>" ×5]. createGzip was called 5 times, one full re-compress per append.
- Output: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/me/rotateFailure.vitest.txt
- Exposure: the live board's five generations are intact today (gzip -t OK on .moe/activity.log.1-5.gz, which span 2026-11-01T11:33Z to now). So this is a guard gap, not a live incident. The trigger is a full disk or a locked file during a rotation, which happens every ~10 MB, about twice a day at today's volume.

FIX DIRECTION
- Compress the live log to a temp file next to it first.
- Only after the gzip stream finishes: unlink the oldest generation, shift the rest, rename the temp to .1.gz, and truncate the live log.
- On any compression failure, unlink the temp and leave the chain and the live log untouched.
- Optionally, skip the rotation attempt for a short interval after a failure, so a persistent failure doesn't re-gzip the whole live log on every append under the activity mutex.
- The existing compressFile tests (util/LogRotator.test.ts) keep passing.

FILES
- packages/moe-daemon/src/util/LogRotator.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/util/LogRotator.rotateFailure.test.ts (new)
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md: sync your own section, `### moe.get_activity_log`. Next to the :3167 retention sentence, or as a Notes bullet, say that a failed rotation keeps every generation and the live log.

Placement: no open row holds these files at filing time.

implementationPlan.description:
Runtime (DoD 1, DoD 2): make LogRotator.rotate() compress first, and change the generations only after the compressed copy is complete. All edits are in packages/moe-daemon/src/util/LogRotator.ts.
(1) rotate(). The temporary file is path.join(dir, `${baseName}.rotating.tmp`). It sits next to the log, never matches the reader's activity.log.<n>.gz pattern (state/activityLog.ts readActivityTail), and is covered by .gitignore's `.moe/activity.log*`. Order:
  a. Remove a leftover temp: fs.rmSync with force, because a crash may have left one.
  b. `await this.compressFile(this.logPath, pending)`.
  c. For i = retentionCount-1 down to 1, rename an existing .i.gz to .(i+1).gz. renameSync replaces its target on POSIX and on Windows (libuv MoveFileEx REPLACE_EXISTING). So the first rename drops the oldest generation, and the explicit unlink of .retentionCount.gz goes away: a failed first rename now loses nothing.
  d. Rename the temp to .1.gz.
  e. Truncate the live log.
  Wrap that whole sequence in one try/catch. On any throw, remove the temp (rmSync force) inside its own try/catch that only logs a cleanup failure at warn, then rethrow the ORIGINAL error. compressFile itself is unchanged, and its tests in util/LogRotator.test.ts must keep passing as they are. Update rotate()'s doc comment to the new order.
(2) rotateIfNeeded(). Add `export const ROTATION_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 60_000` and a private `retryAfter = 0` (epoch ms). At the top: `if (Date.now() < this.retryAfter) return false;`. In the existing catch, set `this.retryAfter = Date.now() + ROTATION_RETRY_DELAY_MS` and add retryInMs to the existing error log. Success, a missing log and a log under the threshold behave exactly as today. rotateIfNeeded still never throws: appendActivity (state/activityLog.ts:96-102) calls it under the activity mutex before every append and relies on that.
Error handling: every failure path ends in the same catch: a compression error or timeout, a failed rename, a failed truncate. The temp is removed, the original error is rethrown and logged by rotateIfNeeded, and the next attempt waits ROTATION_RETRY_DELAY_MS. Keep the change small (about +30/-15 lines). Edit with your own editor tool (Edit on Claude, apply_patch on codex exec), never a shell write (project rail).
implementationPlan.note: rotate() now compresses to activity.log.rotating.tmp first; shifts via rename-replace (no explicit unlink of the oldest), renames tmp to .1.gz, truncates live; any failure removes tmp (warn-only cleanup) and rethrows the original error. rotateIfNeeded gains exported ROTATION_RETRY_DELAY_MS=60_000 and private retryAfter; a failure arms it, and a call inside the window returns false without compressing. compressFile/getRotatedLogs untouched.

Created LogRotator.rotateFailure.test.ts with rows (f1)-(f4): one failing rotation, five failing then one success, retry delay via a Date.now spy (no fake timers), partial-write timeout path via a compressFile spy. Executed in step 4's snapshot gate.

Review only, no file changed. RED proof (merge-base LogRotator.ts + new test file): "Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 4 failed (4)". Rows f2/f3 failed there partly because the old file lacks ROTATION_RETRY_DELAY_MS (NaN clock), so I re-ran in the scratch snapshot with only that constant added to the old file: still 4 failed for the real reasons (f1/f2 "unexpected end of file" = 0-byte .1.gz, f3 createGzip 2x, f4 dest is activity.log.1.gz). Walked: compression error/timeout (f1/f4); rename failure mid-shift and truncate failure are pre-existing classes, out of scope (temp removed, original error rethrown, live log kept; a mid-shift failure leaves .1 missing until the next attempt, truncate failure duplicates once); crash leftover temp removed by rmSync at the start of rotate(); Windows renameSync replaces target, a failing rmSync is caught, warned, and the original error rethrown; retentionCount 1: shift loop skipped, temp renamed over .1.gz; chain gap unchanged. Theoretical: system clock jumping back delays the next rotation (log grows, no data loss); destination open racing a destroyed stream could leave an empty temp, removed next attempt, gitignored. rotateIfNeeded cannot throw (Date.now, existsSync outside try cannot throw; stat+rotate inside); only caller is appendActivity under the activity mutex. compressFile, getRotatedLogs, util/LogRotator.test.ts unchanged; no forbidden pattern in added lines; docs diff is one hunk in ### moe.get_activity_log.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: LogRotator.rotate() first compresses the live activity.log into a temporary file next to it (activity.log.rotating.tmp). It changes the generation chain only after that file is complete: each existing activity.log.<i>.gz moves to <i+1> (each rename replaces its target, so the first drops the oldest), the temporary file becomes activity.log.1.gz, and only then is the live log truncated. Any failure in that sequence removes the temporary file and rethrows, so a failed or timed-out compression leaves every generation and the live log exactly as they were. rotateIfNeeded still swallows the error and returns false. After a failure it skips further attempts for ROTATION_RETRY_DELAY_MS (60 s), so a persistent failure no longer re-reads and re-gzips the whole live log on every append under the activity mutex.
acceptanceCriteria: (f1) One failing rotation keeps .1-.5.gz in place with their seeded content and the live log byte-identical, and leaves no other file in the directory (DoD 1).

(f2) Five failing rotations, each really attempted, keep everything. A later successful one writes the live content to .1.gz, shifts the seeded generations to .2-.5 dropping the oldest, and truncates the live log (DoD 2).
(f3) After a failure, rotateIfNeeded does not compress again until ROTATION_RETRY_DELAY_MS has passed.
(f4) A compression that rejects after a partial write (the timeout path) targets only the temporary file and leaves the chain, the live log and the directory listing unchanged.

The temporary name activity.log.rotating.tmp matches .gitignore's `.moe/activity.log*` and never the reader's `.<n>.gz` pattern. FileWatcher ignores top-level .moe files.
LogRotatorOptions, getRotatedLogs and compressFile are unchanged, and util/LogRotator.test.ts passes unmodified.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Compress in memory with gzipSync: rejected, it blocks the event loop on a ~10 MB log. (2) Keep the shift-first order and roll the renames back on failure: rejected, because compress-first reduces the failure path to one unlink. (3) Unlink the oldest generation first, as today, versus rename-replace: chose rename-replace. Both give the same result on success, but a failed first rename then loses nothing. (4) A compaction pass that heals gaps left by a mid-shift rename failure: out of scope, since it needs a rename to fail, not the compression. (5) The retry delay as a constructor option versus an exported constant: chose the constant; tests drive Date.now through vi.spyOn.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Every activity append runs rotateIfNeeded first, under the activity mutex, so without the retry delay a persistent failure re-gzips the whole live log once per event. With the 30 s compression timeout, that can also stall the queue past its 1000-pending backpressure limit. The reader stops at the first missing generation, so keeping the chain contiguous matters as much as keeping the bytes. LogRotator imports zlib's default export and calls zlib.createGzip at call time, so vi.spyOn(zlib, 'createGzip') reaches it.
planningNotes.risks: (a) A theoretical race: if the destination stream's open had not finished when the compression failed, the cleanup could run first and leave an empty temp. That is harmless (gitignored, not a generation name) and removed by the next attempt; in the test the gzip fails only after the source was read, so the open has finished. (b) A rename failing mid-shift or a truncate failing are pre-existing failure classes; they do not lose the live log, and are out of scope. (c) Tests must not use vi.useFakeTimers; Date.now via vi.spyOn is enough. (d) vitest's restoreAllMocks restores the Date.now and createGzip spies between tests. (e) docs/MCP_SERVER.md is also edited by three open rows: touch only this section's bullet.
